article_content: Rod Stowe has reportedly been dismissed from his position as Fair Trading Commissioner. Two business owners in NSW are facing substantial fines and potential prosecution after Fair Trading uncovered counterfeit phone chargers similar to the one that caused the death of a young mother earlier this year. The Sydney Morning Herald reports that over 260 raids took place this week, and the two shop owners could be fined up to $87,500 and imprisoned for up to two years. Fair Trading also discovered a dozen businesses selling substandard chargers and adapters, and undercover officers found six stalls at Paddy's markets Haymarket and Dapto markets on the NSW south coast. Consumer watchdog boss Rod Stowe is also under scrutiny, with reports suggesting he has been stood down from his position as NSW Fair Trading Commissioner following the death of Sheryl Anne Aldeguer, 28, who was electrocuted by a faulty USB charger at her Gosford home. Daily Mail Australia has learned that Mr Stowe has taken leave just 10 days after it was revealed that the young mother-of-two, who had moved from the Philippines to Australia for work, died as a result of the faulty USB charger that electrocuted her on April 23. This incident prompted NSW Fair Trading to issue a warning against buying counterfeit chargers, with Commissioner Rod Stowe stating that they 'may not meet Australian safety standards' and 'pose a serious risk of electrocution or fire.' However, more than a week later, Mr Stowe has reportedly left his position, although no one has confirmed the Sunday Telegraph's report that he was sacked. Several spokespeople from NSW Fair Trading and The Department of Finance and Services have confirmed that Assistant Commissioner John Tansey has replaced him, but the reason for his sudden appointment remains unclear. Sheryl Aldeguer, 28, died in April due to a faulty phone charger. She is pictured here with her husband, Luigi. Police had warned consumers to bend the pins and discard any counterfeit USB chargers similar to the one that led to the death on the NSW Central Coast. Daily Mail Australia contacted a spokesperson for the Department of Finance and Services, who declined to comment further, stating, 'Fair Trading Commissioner, Rod Stowe, is on leave. During this time, John Tansey will serve as Fair Trading Commissioner.' A police investigation revealed on June 26 that a USB charger, not a laptop as initially suspected, caused Sheryl Aldeguer's death on the NSW Central Coast. The stall owners face fines of $87,500 and/or two years imprisonment. Mr Stowe stated at the time that the penalty was a 'wake-up call to people who buy cheap electronic products without realizing potential hazards.' Fair Trading Electrical Product Safety Expert Lynelle Collins also noted that it had been five years since a similar death caused by a faulty electronic device but emphasized the ongoing risk of further deaths. 'Particularly with the Internet, people can buy items directly from overseas wholesalers that may not meet Australian safety standards,' she said. Meanwhile, two NSW Fair Trading media advisors, when contacted for comment regarding Mr Stowe's 'leave' arrangements, informed Daily Mail Australia that they had been 'instructed' to direct inquiries to Melissah Bell, who is listed as a 'media contact' on the Fair Trading website. Ms Bell stated that Mr Stowe's leave arrangements are a matter for the Office of Finance and Services and declined to comment on whether the leave was indefinite. 'There is nothing more I can tell you at this stage,' she said.
translated_content: Rod Stowe dilaporkan telah diberhentikan dari jabatannya sebagai Komisaris Perdagangan yang Adil. Dua pemilik bisnis di NSW menghadapi denda besar dan potensi penuntutan setelah Fair Trading menemukan pengisi daya telepon palsu yang mirip dengan yang menyebabkan kematian seorang ibu muda awal tahun ini. Sydney Morning Herald melaporkan bahwa lebih dari 260 penggerebekan terjadi minggu ini, dan kedua pemilik toko dapat didenda hingga $87.500 dan dipenjara hingga dua tahun. Fair Trading juga menemukan belasan bisnis yang menjual pengisi daya dan adaptor di bawah standar, dan petugas yang menyamar menemukan enam kios di pasar Paddy's Haymarket dan pasar Dapto di pantai selatan NSW. Kepala pengawas konsumen Rod Stowe juga berada di bawah pengawasan, dengan laporan yang menyatakan bahwa ia telah dinonaktifkan dari jabatannya sebagai Komisaris Perdagangan yang Adil NSW setelah kematian Sheryl Anne Aldeguer, 28 tahun, yang tersetrum oleh pengisi daya USB rusak di rumahnya di Gosford. Daily Mail Australia mengetahui bahwa Mr. Stowe telah mengambil cuti hanya 10 hari setelah terungkap bahwa ibu muda dengan dua anak, yang telah pindah dari Filipina ke Australia untuk bekerja, meninggal akibat pengisi daya USB rusak yang menyetrumnya pada 23 April. Insiden ini mendorong NSW Fair Trading untuk mengeluarkan peringatan agar tidak membeli pengisi daya palsu, dengan Komisaris Rod Stowe menyatakan bahwa produk tersebut 'mungkin tidak memenuhi standar keselamatan Australia' dan 'menimbulkan risiko serius sengatan listrik atau kebakaran'. Namun, lebih dari seminggu kemudian, Mr. Stowe dilaporkan telah meninggalkan jabatannya, meskipun belum ada konfirmasi resmi mengenai laporan dari Sunday Telegraph yang menyatakan bahwa ia telah dipecat. Beberapa juru bicara dari NSW Fair Trading dan Departemen Keuangan dan Layanan telah mengonfirmasi bahwa Asisten Komisaris John Tansey telah menggantikannya, tetapi alasan penunjukannya yang mendadak masih belum jelas. Sheryl Aldeguer, 28 tahun, meninggal dunia pada bulan April akibat pengisi daya telepon yang rusak. Ia terlihat di foto ini bersama suaminya, Luigi. Polisi telah memperingatkan konsumen untuk menekuk pin dan membuang pengisi daya USB palsu yang mirip dengan yang menyebabkan kematian di NSW Central Coast. Daily Mail Australia menghubungi juru bicara Departemen Keuangan dan Layanan, yang menolak memberikan komentar lebih lanjut, dan menyatakan, 'Komisaris Perdagangan yang Adil, Rod Stowe, sedang cuti. Selama masa cuti ini, John Tansey akan bertindak sebagai Komisaris Perdagangan yang Adil.' Investigasi polisi mengungkap pada tanggal 26 Juni bahwa pengisi daya USB, bukan laptop seperti yang semula diduga, menjadi penyebab kematian Sheryl Aldeguer di NSW Central Coast. Para pemilik kios menghadapi denda sebesar $87.500 dan/atau hukuman penjara selama dua tahun. Mr. Stowe menyatakan pada saat itu bahwa hukuman ini adalah 'peringatan bagi masyarakat yang membeli produk elektronik murah tanpa menyadari potensi bahayanya'. Pakar Keselamatan Produk Listrik Fair Trading, Lynelle Collins, juga mencatat bahwa sudah lima tahun sejak kematian serupa akibat perangkat elektronik yang rusak, namun menekankan adanya risiko kematian lebih lanjut. Dia menambahkan, 'Terutama dengan adanya internet, masyarakat dapat membeli barang secara langsung dari pedagang grosir luar negeri yang mungkin tidak memenuhi standar keselamatan Australia.' Sementara itu, dua penasihat media NSW Fair Trading, ketika dihubungi untuk memberikan komentar mengenai status 'cuti' Mr. Stowe, memberi tahu Daily Mail Australia bahwa mereka telah 'diinstruksikan' untuk mengarahkan pertanyaan ke Melissah Bell, yang terdaftar sebagai 'kontak media' di situs web Fair Trading. Ms. Bell menyatakan bahwa status cuti Mr. Stowe adalah wewenang dari Kantor Keuangan dan Layanan, dan menolak berkomentar apakah cuti tersebut bersifat permanen atau tidak. 'Tidak ada informasi lebih lanjut yang dapat saya sampaikan saat ini,' ujarnya.

article_content: If you overindulged this Christmas and are looking to jump on the New Year diet bandwagon, our favorite A-list health guru is here to help. Health advocate Gwyneth Paltrow has unveiled a January detox meal plan, which she promises is 'warming, filling, and doesn't feel like a sacrifice'. While the 41-year-old probably didn't consume as much stuffing and Christmas pudding as many did this festive season, she has joined forces with a nutritionist to create a healthy and cleansing meal plan. It's detox time! Gwyneth Paltrow, an avid foodie, has unveiled a January detox menu, which she promises doesn't feel like a sacrifice. Writing on her site Goop, she says: 'You know we love a good detox here at Goop, and this January is no exception. 'We created detox recipes that won't leave you feeling cold and hungry during the winter months, with guidance from Dr. Alejandro Junger, a specialist on the subject. 'We tested recipes in the test kitchen to create a three-day menu of detox recipes that are warming, filling, and don't feel like a sacrifice. 'We then consulted Dr. Alejandro Junger for information on how to best detox during the cold winter months. Dr. Junger contributed the warm shakes - the rest of the recipes are from the Goop kitchen.' Hard at work: Gwyneth and her team collaborated with a nutritionist to create some healthy recipes for her Goop fans to enjoy. The menu advises detoxers to start the day with room temperature water and lemon, followed by a herbal tea and special shake. Lunch consists of either a balsamic miso root salad or chickpea or carrot soup (bread rolls not included, obviously). If you're feeling peckish in the afternoon, Gwyneth suggests snacking on walnut lentil pate or a handful of nuts before enjoying coconut poached salmon, quinoa stuffed squash, or pan-steamed chicken and broccoli for dinner. 'Adjust the times to your schedule and the meals to your taste,' advises the actress. What, no carbs? Plenty of herbal teas, salads, soups, and oily fish feature on Gwyneth's menu. Foodies will be delighted to hear that this winter detox is much less strict than ones Gwyneth and her team have created in the past. 'Our winter detox has looser guidelines and restrictions than ones we’ve done in the past,' she adds, 'but here is what we’re avoiding: dairy, gluten, shellfish, anything processed (including all soy products), nightshades (potatoes, tomatoes, peppers, and eggplant), condiments, sugar, alcohol, caffeine, and soda,' she writes. The mother-of-two is well-known for her strict health regime and even released her own cookbook, 'It's All Good', in 2012. Wise words: Gwyneth, who released a cookbook with her dietary tips, writes a weekly lifestyle blog. According to the book's synopsis, after a gruelling schedule and overindulgence in 2011, Gwyneth felt fatigued and faint, and a trip to the doctor later revealed that she was anaemic, vitamin D deficient, and that her stress levels were sky high. Her doctor prescribed an elimination diet banning coffee, alcohol, sugar, eggs, wheat, meat, and processed food to clear out her system and help her body heal. Now we can ALL look like Gwyneth: The detox eliminates dairy, gluten, shellfish, anything processed (including all soy products), nightshades (potatoes, tomatoes, peppers, and eggplant), condiments, sugar, alcohol, caffeine, and soda.

article_content: A protester who 'harassed and stalked' former education secretary Sir Gavin Williamson has been spared jail but received a restraining order. The Conservative MP stated he felt 'incredibly threatened' by Simon Parry, who 'persistently followed' him near the Houses of Parliament. Parry, 45, was found guilty of stalking and given a 10-week suspended prison sentence. He was also prohibited from contacting or being near the South Staffordshire MP for five years. Parry had followed Sir Gavin on two occasions near the Houses of Parliament on May 24 and June 14. He voiced anti-vaccination opinions and spoke of conspiracy theories. At Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday, he received a 10-week prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, after being convicted last month of one count of stalking. Sentencing Parry, deputy chief magistrate Tan Ikram stated: 'It is an aggravated factor that public servants who are trying their best are harassed and stalked in this way.' 'It deters good people from entering public service.' He continued: 'You do not fully accept that you're wrong and think that this is an appropriate way to challenge Members of Parliament.' 'Let me be clear, it is not.' Parry, from Walworth, south London, was ordered not to contact Sir Gavin or his office or knowingly be within 100 meters of him. Mr. Ikram added: 'It is necessary and proportionate to deal with the risks in this case.' Follow BBC West Midlands on Facebook, X, and Instagram. article_content: From fizzy drinks to chocolate, everyone has their vices, but for 19-year-old Allison, her craving is for rubber shavings. For the past six years, Allison from Atlanta, Georgia, has consumed rubber car tires as her preferred daily snack. Allison explains that she finds the chewiness appealing: 'The texture of the rubber pieces is like beef jerky. It’s a workout for your jaw.' Allison's strange addiction began when she started chewing rubber as a child, initially munching on the feet of her dolls. She admits to experiencing stomach issues but struggles to break her habit. Allison keeps bowls of rubber shavings around her house for snacking whenever she feels the urge. Although she isn't concerned about the chemicals in the rubber, she ensures the tires are washed before consumption. As a child, she chewed on her dolls' feet. After growing tired of that, she switched to chewing gum. One day, she tried tire shavings, drawn to their potential chewiness, and hasn't stopped since. She now consumes two feet of shavings daily, totaling 50 full tires since her addiction began. Allison states: 'It does taste chemically, but it's amazing.' Allison keeps shavings in small bowls around her home, allowing her to snack on them throughout the day. According to Allison, the tire shavings provide a 'great workout' for her jaw. If Allison can't find tire shavings, she substitutes with rubber bands or rubber glue. Despite her love for rubber, she acknowledges that it frequently causes digestive problems. Her fiance, Sammy, who works at a tire factory, became so concerned that he urged her to see a doctor. Allison eventually underwent several x-rays to ensure there was no permanent damage to her stomach, all of which came back clear. However, the doctor warned her about the potential risk of developing cancer from the chemicals she ingests daily. Since then, Allison has reduced her intake but still finds it difficult to completely overcome her addiction. Allison says she isn't worried about the chemicals in the rubber, but she takes the precaution of washing the tires before eating them. Sammy, her worried fiance who works in a tire factory, encouraged her to seek medical attention. Allison, 19, from Atlanta, Georgia, consulted Dr. Melvin Glover to check for any permanent damage to her stomach. Having consumed a total of 50 tires since her addiction started, Allison had an x-ray to assess her body's ability to cope with her rubber consumption. Allison is featured in an episode of TLC's My Strange Addiction, which also highlights other women with unusual eating obsessions, ranging from tape to cat hair and vapor rub. Danielle, 33, from San Antonio, Texas, shared her vapor rub addiction on the program. She uses inhalers, patches, candles, and rubs to satisfy her craving, and even adds the gel to her morning tea. 'I like to feel it melt in the back of my throat,' she explained.

article_content: By Chris Greenwood and Andrew Meldrum: A 30-year-old man used specialist computer software to spy on women undressing. An IT expert installed spy software on women’s computers to watch them undress. Andrew Meldrum, 30, an IT expert, posed as a helpful friend who would fix their laptops. The university student abused their trust to stealthily watch them during their most intimate moments. Police discovered he had amassed more than 11,000 pictures of his two victims, many of them naked, after secretly taking control of their computers. Yesterday, a judge said he was sure the 'Peeping Tom' was acting solely to feed his own 'sexual gratification'. However, he allowed him to walk free from court after handing him a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for two years. It is believed to be the first time anyone in the UK has been convicted of abusing webcams to spy on others in this way. The case echoes the spying activities of GCHQ, which were revealed earlier this year to have accessed the cameras and microphones of computers without the owners’ permission. Meldrum’s actions were uncovered when one of his two young female victims realized something was wrong with her computer. In a panic, Meldrum immediately sent her a text saying, 'Please don’t call the police'. She contacted the police, and investigators discovered he had planted a specialist program on their laptops while pretending to fix other problems. It allowed him to watch them around the clock from his home via the computers’ webcams without their knowledge. He even persuaded one of the women to keep the laptop at the end of her bed so it was in a 'better position for watching movies'. In fact, it gave him a prime spot for watching her being intimate with her boyfriend, Woolwich Crown Court was told. The women were horrified when police showed them intimate photos of themselves in front of their bedroom mirrors, often naked or in their underwear. In one case, the software had been installed for 15 months and was set up to take a photograph every two seconds and transmit it to Meldrum. Prosecutor James Vine said: 'If you asked most people what a voyeur was, they’d probably tell you it was another word for Peeping Tom. They would be right. That is exactly what this case is about, albeit a very modern version for the technological age. Andrew Meldrum does not peep through keyholes or curtains. He is rather more sophisticated than that.' The two victims, who cannot be named for legal reasons, tearfully comforted one another as he was sentenced yesterday. Recorder Mark Heywood said Meldrum ‘surreptitiously’ installed the software which even allowed him to watch the women on his mobile phone. He told Meldrum he ‘abused these people’s trust and confidence’. Shila Whitehead, defending Meldrum, said he had lost his job in IT and a place at Goldsmiths University because of his crimes. She added: 'He is extremely remorseful, and he accepts he violated their privacy. He previously turned to gambling and alcohol and has huge debts.' Meldrum, of Lewisham, South-East London, was convicted of two counts of voyeurism by a jury and admitted a further three counts of unauthorised computer access. He was told he would be supervised for two years and must undergo 20 sessions aimed at addressing his behaviour. He was ordered to sign the sex offenders’ register for ten years and pay £2,100 in costs, and he was told he cannot use a computer unless his activities are monitored. One of the victims told ITV news: 'It makes you question your trust in people and makes you question how you live your daily life, and what you do in your home daily, knowing that someone is constantly watching you.' When asked about the breach of trust she had experienced, she said: 'It’s just quite difficult really to know who to trust.'

Dalam satu kasus, perangkat lunak itu telah diinstal selama 15 bulan dan diatur untuk mengambil foto setiap dua detik dan mengirimkannya ke Meldrum. Jaksa James Vine mengatakan: 'Jika Anda bertanya kepada kebanyakan orang apa itu voyeur, mereka mungkin akan memberi tahu Anda bahwa itu adalah kata lain untuk Peeping Tom. Mereka benar. Kedua korban, yang tidak dapat disebutkan namanya karena alasan hukum, saling menghibur dengan berlinang air mata saat dia dijatuhi hukuman kemarin. Shila Whitehead, yang membela Meldrum, mengatakan dia telah kehilangan pekerjaannya di bidang TI dan tempat di Goldsmiths University karena kejahatannya. Dia menambahkan: 'Dia sangat menyesal, dan dia menerima bahwa dia melanggar privasi mereka. Dia sebelumnya beralih ke perjudian dan alkohol dan memiliki utang besar.' Meldrum, dari Lewisham, London Tenggara, dinyatakan bersalah atas dua dakwaan voyeurisme oleh juri dan mengakui tiga dakwaan lebih lanjut atas akses komputer tanpa izin. Dia diperintahkan untuk menandatangani daftar pelaku kejahatan seksual selama sepuluh tahun dan membayar biaya sebesar £2.100, dan dia diberi tahu bahwa dia tidak dapat menggunakan komputer kecuali aktivitasnya dipantau. Salah satu korban mengatakan kepada berita ITV: 'Itu membuat Anda mempertanyakan kepercayaan Anda pada orang lain dan membuat Anda mempertanyakan bagaimana Anda menjalani kehidupan sehari-hari, dan apa yang Anda lakukan di rumah setiap hari, mengetahui bahwa seseorang terus-menerus mengawasi Anda.' Ketika ditanya tentang pelanggaran kepercayaan yang dia alami, dia berkata: 'Sulit sekali untuk mengetahui siapa yang bisa dipercaya.'

article_content: Lord Coe has unveiled his manifesto for the presidency of the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF), promising to address the issue of athletes switching nationality for financial gain. Coe, likely to compete against Sergey Bubka in the upcoming election, emphasizes making it more attractive for athletes to represent their country of origin. This follows criticism of Team GB's selection of recently naturalized citizens before the London 2012 Olympics. Lord Coe aims to succeed current IAAF president Lamine Diack when he steps down next year. His manifesto includes: - Reforming the global athletics calendar and introducing city-center 'street athletics' competitions. - Maximizing commercial growth and focusing on engaging young people. - Enhancing resources for anti-doping efforts and establishing a new IAAF ethics department. - Modifying the IAAF internal structure to provide athletes with a stronger voice. Coe stated, 'There is a clear problem regarding the transfer of allegiance, particularly when it is driven solely by financial incentives. It is crucial for the sport to have a thorough discussion on this matter and take appropriate action. There is considerable concern across many continents about the need to resolve this issue.' The former Olympic champion, 58, currently holds positions such as chairman of the British Olympic Association, executive chairman of CSM Sports and Entertainment, a global ambassador for Nike, and an advisor to PruHealth and Deutsche Bank UK. He assures that he would avoid any conflict of interest, as he did during his chairmanship of London 2012, if appointed by the IAAF. Coe, currently a vice-president of the IAAF, is running to succeed Lamine Diack, who is retiring in August. Coe, who led the London 2012 organizing committee, commented, 'To many both inside and outside of our sport, our calendar appears fragmented, lacks a cohesive narrative, and lacks the necessary elements to create excitement and cultivate a loyal fanbase.' 'Many fans are unaware of when the athletics season begins and ends, and why it shifts from the USA to Europe to Asia and back. A streamlined calendar is essential for promotion, marketing, athlete development, and member federation development, and we must address this.' 'We need to be more innovative in how we showcase our sport to the world, both at venues and on screen. We should seriously consider an 'IAAF Street Athletics' circuit to reach new audiences and establish a new IAAF division focused solely on engaging young people, especially through social media.'
translated_content: Lord Coe telah mengungkapkan manifesto-nya untuk jabatan presiden Asosiasi Federasi Atletik Internasional (IAAF), berjanji untuk mengatasi isu atlet yang beralih kewarganegaraan demi keuntungan finansial. Coe, yang kemungkinan akan bersaing dengan Sergey Bubka dalam pemilihan mendatang, menekankan untuk membuat atlet lebih tertarik untuk mewakili negara asal mereka. Hal ini menyusul kritik terhadap pemilihan warga negara yang baru dinaturalisasi oleh Tim GB sebelum Olimpiade London 2012. Lord Coe bertujuan untuk menggantikan presiden IAAF saat ini, Lamine Diack, ketika dia mengundurkan diri tahun depan. Manifesto-nya meliputi: - Mereformasi kalender atletik global dan memperkenalkan kompetisi 'atletik jalanan' di pusat kota. - Memaksimalkan pertumbuhan komersial dan fokus pada melibatkan kaum muda. - Meningkatkan sumber daya untuk upaya anti-doping dan membentuk departemen etika IAAF yang baru. - Memodifikasi struktur internal IAAF untuk memberikan suara yang lebih kuat kepada para atlet. Coe menyatakan, 'Ada isu yang jelas mengenai pengalihan kesetiaan, terutama ketika didorong semata-mata oleh insentif keuangan. Sangat penting bagi olahraga ini untuk melakukan diskusi menyeluruh tentang isu ini dan mengambil tindakan yang tepat. Ada kekhawatiran yang cukup besar di banyak benua tentang perlunya menyelesaikan isu ini.' Mantan juara Olimpiade berusia 58 tahun ini saat ini memegang jabatan seperti ketua Asosiasi Olimpiade Inggris, ketua eksekutif CSM Sports and Entertainment, duta global untuk Nike, dan penasihat untuk PruHealth dan Deutsche Bank UK. Dia meyakinkan bahwa dia akan menghindari konflik kepentingan apa pun, seperti yang dia lakukan selama masa jabatannya sebagai ketua Olimpiade London 2012, jika ditunjuk oleh IAAF. Coe, yang saat ini menjabat sebagai wakil presiden IAAF, mencalonkan diri untuk menggantikan Lamine Diack, yang pensiun pada bulan Agustus. Coe, yang memimpin komite penyelenggara Olimpiade London 2012, berkomentar, 'Bagi banyak orang baik di dalam maupun di luar olahraga kita, kalender kita tampak terfragmentasi, tidak memiliki narasi yang kohesif, dan tidak memiliki elemen yang diperlukan untuk menciptakan kegembiraan dan menumbuhkan basis penggemar yang setia.' 'Banyak penggemar tidak menyadari kapan musim atletik dimulai dan berakhir, dan mengapa ia berpindah dari AS ke Eropa ke Asia dan kembali lagi. Kalender yang efisien sangat penting untuk promosi, pemasaran, pengembangan atlet, dan pengembangan federasi anggota, dan kita harus mengatasi hal ini.' 'Kita perlu lebih inovatif dalam cara kita memamerkan olahraga kita kepada dunia, baik di tempat maupun di layar. article_content: A trial to decide who will inherit the $300 million estate of reclusive copper mining heiress Huguette Clark has been delayed for two days in a last-ditch effort to reach a settlement. Attorneys stated that jury selection, originally scheduled to begin on Tuesday, has been postponed until Thursday to allow more time for negotiations. The office of the New York Attorney General, Eric Schneiderman, is attempting to broker a settlement, according to attorneys speaking to NBC News. Previous attempts by his office's Charities Bureau have been unsuccessful, as Clark's relatives, who were excluded from the will, have not reached an agreement with the beneficiaries. The case, involving over 60 lawyers, concerns the final will of Clark, who owned lavish properties from New York's Fifth Avenue to the California coast but chose to spend her last 20 years in a Manhattan hospital. She passed away in 2011 at the age of 104. The dispute pits nearly two dozen of Clark's distant relatives against a goddaughter, the hospital, a nurse, doctors, a lawyer, an accountant, and other professionals and aides who benefited from her April 2005 will, which left nothing to her family. Gifts to Clark's primary nurse included several Manhattan apartments and a $1.2 million Stradivarius violin. Her primary doctor received cash Christmas presents totaling $500,000, among other gifts. The hospital received hundreds of thousands of dollars in cash and a $3.5 million painting by French pre-Impressionist Edouard Manet. 'The persons and institution named herein as beneficiaries of my estate are the true objects of my bounty,' the will stated, noting that the childless, briefly married Clark had had only 'minimal contacts' with her relatives over the years. However, the will was signed just six weeks after another version, which left almost all her money to the family members, descendants of her half-siblings. The relatives claim that a group of hospital executives, medical professionals, and Clark's lawyer and accountant exploited their access to the secluded, elderly heiress to manipulate their way into her millions of dollars. The beneficiaries argue that Clark was simply a generous woman who wanted to reward those who helped her. Clark's father, U.S. Senator William A. Clark, was one of the wealthiest Americans of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He served as a senator from Montana, where he initially made his fortune from copper mines. His business empire expanded to include building a Western rail line and establishing a Nevada railroad town called Las Vegas. Clark County is named after him. The trial will determine only the validity of Huguette Clark's April 2005 will. However, testimony might also examine the expensive gifts her caregivers and advisors received during her lifetime. 'There may be some connection between gift-giving and undue influence in the will,' Manhattan Surrogate's Court Judge Nora Anderson said at a pretrial hearing. Before the trial, a new biography about Clark was released, offering intriguing details about the French-born heiress who was fascinated by life-like dolls and building miniature castles, often spending thousands of dollars on them. The book, Empty Mansions: The Mysterious Life of Huguette Clark and the Spending of a Great American Fortune by Bill Dedman and one of Clark's relatives, Paul Clark Newell Jr., reveals the fascinating family known for staying out of the limelight. According to reports, one of the few people who visited Clark at her apartments in the 1950s said that a long gallery was lined with dolls, each seated on its own luxurious armchair. One of Ms. Clark's rare outings was to attend Christian Dior fashion shows to find clothes for her dolls. The heiress was also obsessed with building miniature models. A lover of Japanese culture, although she never traveled there, Clark paid for someone to visit Japan to photograph and document the specifications of the castles she wanted to build from her mansion. While she stayed at the hospital, her three lavish homes remained empty: the $100 million Bellosguardo estate, a $24 million country house in Connecticut, and a $100 million co-op, the largest apartment on Fifth Avenue overlooking Central Park. She inherited her wealth from her father, Montana Senator William Clark, and his copper mines but considered her great wealth 'a menace to happiness'. When she died two weeks before her 105th birthday, the only people present at her burial were funeral home employees.
translated_content: Sidang untuk memutuskan siapa yang akan mewarisi harta $300 juta milik pewaris tambang tembaga tertutup, Huguette Clark, telah ditunda selama dua hari sebagai upaya terakhir untuk mencapai penyelesaian. Pengacara menyatakan bahwa pemilihan juri, yang awalnya dijadwalkan dimulai pada hari Selasa, telah ditunda hingga Kamis untuk memberikan waktu lebih banyak untuk negosiasi. Kantor Jaksa Agung New York, Eric Schneiderman, sedang berupaya menengahi penyelesaian, menurut pernyataan pengacara kepada NBC News. Upaya sebelumnya oleh Biro Amal kantornya tidak berhasil, karena kerabat Clark, yang tidak mendapatkan warisan dalam surat wasiat, belum mencapai kesepakatan dengan para penerima manfaat. Kasus ini, yang melibatkan lebih dari 60 pengacara, berkaitan dengan surat wasiat terakhir Clark, yang memiliki properti mewah dari Fifth Avenue New York hingga pantai California tetapi memilih untuk menghabiskan 20 tahun terakhirnya di rumah sakit Manhattan. Dia meninggal pada tahun 2011 pada usia 104 tahun. Sengketa ini mempertemukan hampir dua lusin kerabat jauh Clark dengan seorang putri baptis, rumah sakit, seorang perawat, dokter, pengacara, akuntan, dan profesional serta asisten lainnya yang mendapat manfaat dari surat wasiat April 2005, yang tidak memberikan apa pun kepada keluarganya. Hadiah untuk perawat utama Clark termasuk beberapa apartemen di Manhattan dan sebuah biola Stradivarius senilai $1,2 juta. Dokter pribadinya menerima hadiah Natal berupa uang tunai dengan total $500.000, di antara hadiah-hadiah lainnya. Rumah sakit menerima ratusan ribu dolar dalam bentuk tunai dan sebuah lukisan senilai $3,5 juta karya pelukis pra-Impresionis Prancis, Edouard Manet. ‘Orang-orang dan lembaga yang disebutkan di sini sebagai penerima manfaat dari harta saya adalah tujuan sebenarnya dari kemurahan hati saya,’ demikian pernyataan surat wasiat tersebut, yang mencatat bahwa Clark yang tidak memiliki anak dan hanya menikah sebentar, hanya memiliki ‘kontak minimal’ dengan kerabatnya selama bertahun-tahun. Namun, surat wasiat itu ditandatangani hanya enam minggu setelah versi lain, yang memberikan hampir semua uangnya kepada anggota keluarga, keturunan dari saudara tiri nya. Kerabat mengklaim bahwa sekelompok eksekutif rumah sakit, profesional medis, serta pengacara dan akuntan Clark mengeksploitasi akses mereka ke pewaris lansia yang terpencil itu untuk memanipulasi mereka agar mendapatkan jutaan dolar miliknya. Para penerima manfaat berpendapat bahwa Clark hanyalah seorang wanita dermawan yang ingin menghargai mereka yang telah membantunya. Ayah Clark, Senator AS William A. Clark, adalah salah satu orang Amerika terkaya pada akhir abad ke-19 dan awal abad ke-20. Dia menjabat sebagai senator dari Montana, tempat dia awalnya mendapatkan kekayaannya dari tambang tembaga. Kerajaan bisnisnya berkembang hingga mencakup pembangunan jalur kereta api Barat dan pendirian kota kereta api Nevada bernama Las Vegas. Clark County dinamai untuk menghormatinya. Persidangan ini hanya akan menentukan keabsahan surat wasiat Huguette Clark tertanggal April 2005. Namun, kesaksian juga dapat memeriksa hadiah mahal yang diterima oleh para pengasuh dan penasihatnya selama masa hidupnya. ‘Mungkin ada hubungan antara pemberian hadiah dan pengaruh tidak wajar dalam surat wasiat,’ kata Hakim Pengadilan Surrogate Manhattan, Nora Anderson, pada sidang pra-persidangan. Menjelang persidangan, sebuah biografi baru tentang Clark dirilis, yang menawarkan rincian menarik tentang pewaris kelahiran Prancis yang terpesona oleh boneka-boneka yang tampak hidup dan pembangunan istana-istana mini, sering kali menghabiskan ribuan dolar untuk itu. Buku, Empty Mansions: The Mysterious Life of Huguette Clark and the Spending of a Great American Fortune oleh Bill Dedman dan salah satu kerabat Clark, Paul Clark Newell Jr., mengungkap keluarga menarik yang dikenal karena menghindari sorotan. Menurut laporan, salah satu dari sedikit orang yang mengunjungi Clark di apartemennya pada tahun 1950-an mengatakan bahwa sebuah galeri panjang dipenuhi dengan boneka, masing-masing duduk di kursi berlengan mewah. Salah satu kegiatan langka Ms. Clark adalah menghadiri peragaan busana Christian Dior untuk mencari pakaian bagi boneka-bonekanya. Pewaris itu juga terobsesi dengan pembangunan model miniatur. Sebagai pecinta budaya Jepang, meskipun dia tidak pernah bepergian ke sana, Clark membayar seseorang untuk mengunjungi Jepang untuk memotret dan mendokumentasikan spesifikasi istana yang ingin dia bangun dari rumahnya. Saat dia dirawat di rumah sakit, ketiga rumah mewahnya tetap kosong: perkebunan Bellosguardo senilai $100 juta, sebuah rumah pedesaan senilai $24 juta di Connecticut, dan sebuah apartemen senilai $100 juta, apartemen terbesar di Fifth Avenue yang menghadap Central Park. Dia mewarisi kekayaannya dari ayahnya, Senator Montana William Clark, dan tambang-tambang tembaganya, tetapi menganggap kekayaan besarnya sebagai ‘ancaman bagi kebahagiaan’. Ketika dia meninggal dua minggu sebelum ulang tahunnya yang ke-105, satu-satunya orang yang hadir pada pemakamannya adalah karyawan rumah duka.

article_content: After spending two years in a coma, a woman was given a touching final farewell by her family. Her life support was turned off just hours after she was married. He Jingjing and her fiance, Lu Lai, from Guangdong in southeast China, had a bright future ahead in 2011. Both had secured excellent positions in the Guangzhou local government. They had recently purchased a home and were planning their wedding. Lu Lai married his fiance shortly before her life support was discontinued. Their dreams of a long and happy life were tragically cut short when He Jingjing became ill at work. She fell into a coma on the way to the hospital and never regained consciousness. Two years later, her family gathered at her bedside to celebrate her 28th birthday with a cake. They then held a wedding ceremony, fulfilling the couple's desire to marry. Her organs will be donated to help those in need. Lu Lai stated he was glad she would help others live. He added that she would live on in his heart forever, regardless of whether she lived on in others. He will always miss her. Lu Lai recalled the events leading up to his bride-to-be's illness, saying that they were working overtime to save money for a special wedding. She was feeling unwell but did not want to stop working. One day, he received a call saying she had collapsed at her computer and had been taken to the hospital. He was told she had stopped breathing on the way and had to be resuscitated. At the hospital, he learned she was alive but later realized she had suffered permanent brain damage. There was nothing that could be done. Her father, Fang Lu, expressed his grief, saying she was a wonderful, vibrant young woman. He mentioned that she was always prepared to be an organ donor, and through this, part of her would live on and help others. As their only child, they wanted to share one last special moment together. He Jingjing's family paid tribute to their daughter and fiance, who slipped into a coma.

article_content: Despite the United States' refusal to grant a visa, a high-ranking Iranian official stated Saturday that Iran stands by its choice of Hamid Aboutalebi as its ambassador to the United Nations, according to Iranian state television. The White House has informed Iran that Aboutalebi will not receive a visa due to his connections to the 1979 seizure of the U.S. Embassy in Tehran. However, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters in Tehran, as reported by state broadcaster Press TV, that Aboutalebi remains their candidate and they are pursuing the matter through diplomatic channels. Iranian lawmaker Hossein Naqavi Hosseini told the state news agency IRNA that the U.S. is obligated to issue visas in its role as host of the UN headquarters in New York. The White House is still considering a bill passed by Congress this week that would prevent Aboutalebi from entering the United States. Aboutalebi was a member of the Muslim Students Following the Imam's Line, the group responsible for seizing the embassy on November 4, 1979, and holding 52 Americans hostage for 444 days. He is an experienced diplomat who has served as Iran's ambassador to various countries, including Australia, Belgium, Italy, and the European Union. He has also held prominent positions in the Iranian Foreign Ministry. Currently, he works in President Hassan Rouhani's political affairs office and is considered a close associate of the Iranian leader, who is generally seen as a moderate with a reform-oriented agenda. In an interview with Iranian media, Aboutalebi stated that he worked as a translator and negotiator but denied participating in the initial occupation of the embassy. Abbas Abdi, one of the leaders of the U.S. Embassy takeover, exclusively told CNN from Tehran that 'Mr. Aboutalebi was not in Tehran during the initial invasion.' Abdi, now a reformist journalist, said Aboutalebi has 'no relation to the decision-making team, the group who invaded and those who continued the hostage captivity in Iran.' The selection of Aboutalebi could potentially complicate U.S. President Barack Obama's efforts to re-engage with Tehran following Rouhani's election and to negotiate a comprehensive agreement with five other global powers to limit Iran's nuclear program. When asked Friday whether the issue surrounding Aboutalebi would impact nuclear talks, U.S. State Department spokeswoman Jen Psaki told reporters that it had not affected discussions held this week. She declined to provide specific reasons for the visa refusal but stated that the United States had been 'very clear ... with the Iranians that this nomination is not viable.' Hamid Babaei, a spokesperson for the Iranian mission to the United Nations, described the U.S. decision as 'regrettable' and 'in contravention of international law, the obligation of the host country and the inherent right of sovereign member states to designate their representatives to the United Nations.' Because there are no formal diplomatic relations between the United States and Iran, the U.N. mission is Tehran's only diplomatic presence in the United States and has facilitated unofficial communication between the two nations. The action taken this week is unusual, considering the United States is obligated to grant entry visas to representatives of U.N. member states under a 1947 agreement with the international organization. CNN's Laura Bernardini, Elise Labott, and Richard Roth contributed to this report.
translated_content: Meskipun Amerika Serikat menolak memberikan visa, seorang pejabat tinggi Iran menyatakan pada hari Sabtu bahwa Iran tetap pada pilihannya, Hamid Aboutalebi, sebagai duta besar mereka untuk Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa, menurut laporan televisi pemerintah Iran. Gedung Putih telah memberitahu Iran bahwa Aboutalebi tidak akan menerima visa karena keterkaitannya dengan penyitaan Kedutaan Besar AS di Teheran pada tahun 1979. Namun, Wakil Menteri Luar Negeri Iran, Abbas Araghchi, menyampaikan kepada wartawan di Teheran, seperti yang dilaporkan oleh penyiar pemerintah Press TV, bahwa Aboutalebi tetap menjadi kandidat mereka dan mereka sedang mengupayakan penyelesaian masalah ini melalui saluran diplomatik. Anggota parlemen Iran, Hossein Naqavi Hosseini, mengatakan kepada kantor berita pemerintah IRNA bahwa AS berkewajiban mengeluarkan visa karena perannya sebagai tuan rumah markas besar PBB di New York. Gedung Putih masih mempertimbangkan rancangan undang-undang yang disahkan oleh Kongres minggu ini, yang akan melarang Aboutalebi memasuki Amerika Serikat. Aboutalebi adalah anggota kelompok Muslim Students Following the Imam's Line, yang bertanggung jawab atas penyitaan kedutaan pada 4 November 1979, dan menyandera 52 warga Amerika selama 444 hari. Dia adalah seorang diplomat berpengalaman yang pernah menjabat sebagai duta besar Iran untuk berbagai negara, termasuk Australia, Belgia, Italia, dan Uni Eropa. Dia juga pernah memegang posisi penting di Kementerian Luar Negeri Iran. Saat ini, ia bekerja di kantor urusan politik Presiden Hassan Rouhani dan dianggap sebagai orang dekat pemimpin Iran, yang umumnya dipandang sebagai tokoh moderat dengan agenda reformis. Dalam wawancara dengan media Iran, Aboutalebi menyatakan bahwa ia bekerja sebagai penerjemah dan negosiator, tetapi membantah terlibat dalam pendudukan awal kedutaan. Abbas Abdi, salah satu pemimpin penyitaan Kedutaan Besar AS, secara eksklusif mengatakan kepada CNN dari Teheran bahwa 'Tuan Aboutalebi tidak berada di Teheran selama invasi awal tersebut.' Abdi, yang sekarang berprofesi sebagai jurnalis reformis, mengatakan bahwa Aboutalebi 'tidak memiliki hubungan dengan tim pengambil keputusan, kelompok yang menyerbu, maupun mereka yang melanjutkan penyanderaan di Iran'. Pemilihan Aboutalebi berpotensi mempersulit upaya Presiden AS, Barack Obama, untuk menjalin kembali hubungan dengan Teheran setelah terpilihnya Rouhani, serta upaya untuk menegosiasikan perjanjian komprehensif dengan lima kekuatan global lainnya untuk membatasi program nuklir Iran. Ketika ditanya pada hari Jumat apakah masalah seputar Aboutalebi akan mempengaruhi pembicaraan nuklir, juru bicara Departemen Luar Negeri AS, Jen Psaki, mengatakan kepada wartawan bahwa hal itu tidak mempengaruhi diskusi yang diadakan minggu ini. Dia menolak memberikan alasan spesifik atas penolakan visa tersebut, tetapi menyatakan bahwa Amerika Serikat telah 'sangat jelas... kepada Iran bahwa pencalonan ini tidak layak'. Hamid Babaei, juru bicara misi Iran untuk Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa, menggambarkan keputusan AS tersebut sebagai 'sesuatu yang disesalkan' dan 'bertentangan dengan hukum internasional, kewajiban negara tuan rumah, dan hak negara-negara anggota berdaulat untuk menunjuk perwakilan mereka ke Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa.' Karena tidak ada hubungan diplomatik formal antara Amerika Serikat dan Iran, misi PBB adalah satu-satunya perwakilan diplomatik Teheran di Amerika Serikat dan telah memfasilitasi komunikasi tidak resmi antara kedua negara. Tindakan yang diambil minggu ini terbilang tidak lazim, mengingat Amerika Serikat berkewajiban memberikan visa masuk kepada perwakilan negara-negara anggota PBB berdasarkan perjanjian tahun 1947 dengan organisasi internasional tersebut. Laura Bernardini, Elise Labott, dan Richard Roth dari CNN berkontribusi pada laporan ini.

article_content: In Sanford, Florida, the investigation into Trayvon Martin's death continues as his parents advocate for justice in Washington. Martin's mother, Sybrina Fulton, expressed her sorrow and determination to seek justice at a forum on racial profiling and 'stand your ground' laws. His father, Tracy Martin, also vowed to continue fighting for justice. Trayvon Martin, an African-American, died on February 26 after being shot by George Zimmerman, a Hispanic neighborhood watch volunteer, who had reported Martin as suspicious. Zimmerman remains unarrested, fueling outrage and debate. The Martin family lawyer, Benjamin Crump, believes racial profiling led to Martin's death. Zimmerman's family denies accusations of racism. Representative Frederica Wilson described Martin as a victim of a flawed police investigation, suggesting incompetence or mismanagement. She called for Zimmerman's immediate arrest for his own safety. Members of Congress discussed the case on the House floor, emphasizing the need for a fair hearing. Speaker John Boehner acknowledged the tragedy but deferred to ongoing state and federal investigations. Special Prosecutor Angela Corey is seeking 'ear-witnesses' to ascertain what transpired, noting that the public outcry complicates her role. Zimmerman claims self-defense, asserting Martin attacked him. Martin was returning from a store with Skittles and iced tea when the incident occurred. Investigators are examining allegations that Zimmerman used a racial slur during the 911 call preceding the shooting, but CNN's review yielded no consensus. Zimmerman reportedly told police that Martin punched him before the shooting, an account corroborated by police. Neighbors reported hearing screams, and two women recalled finding Zimmerman near Martin's body after the shooting. One woman stated that Zimmerman appeared to be standing over Martin's body without providing aid. Police reports indicated Zimmerman had injuries consistent with his account. Authorities cited Florida's 'stand your ground' law as a reason for not arresting Zimmerman initially, sparking renewed debate over the law. A friend of Zimmerman, Joe Oliver, said Zimmerman is remorseful and that race was not a factor in the incident. The Martin family insists Zimmerman racially profiled and shot their son and advocate for changes to gun laws. Attorney Crump cited 911 tapes, phone records, and testimony from Martin's girlfriend as evidence against Zimmerman. Crump also criticized attempts to 'demonize' Martin by referencing a school suspension related to marijuana residue. Sybrina Fulton decried the efforts to tarnish her son's reputation. The city administrator is working with the Department of Justice to establish independent oversight of resident complaints about the Sanford Police. Zimmerman has reportedly suffered from post-traumatic stress disorder, depression, and insomnia since the shooting. CNN contributors Eric Marrapodi, Ed Payne, Kim Segal, Greg Morrison, John Couwels and Vivian Kuo contributed to this report.

Para penyidik sedang memeriksa tuduhan bahwa Zimmerman menggunakan hinaan rasial saat melakukan panggilan 911 sebelum penembakan terjadi, tetapi hasil peninjauan oleh CNN tidak mencapai mufakat. Seorang wanita menyatakan bahwa Zimmerman tampak berdiri di atas tubuh Martin tanpa memberikan pertolongan. Pihak berwenang menyebutkan hukum 'pertahankan diri' Florida sebagai alasan mengapa Zimmerman tidak segera ditangkap, dan hal ini memicu perdebatan baru tentang hukum tersebut. Seorang teman Zimmerman, Joe Oliver, mengatakan bahwa Zimmerman menyesali kejadian tersebut dan bahwa ras bukanlah faktor yang memicu insiden itu. Keluarga Martin bersikeras bahwa Zimmerman melakukan profiling rasial dan menembak putra mereka, dan mereka mengadvokasi perubahan terhadap undang-undang tentang kepemilikan senjata. Pengacara Crump mengutip rekaman panggilan 911, catatan telepon, dan kesaksian dari pacar Martin sebagai bukti yang memberatkan Zimmerman. Crump juga mengkritik upaya untuk 'mencoreng' nama baik Martin dengan mengungkit penangguhan dirinya dari sekolah terkait dengan residu ganja. Sybrina Fulton mengecam upaya-upaya yang bertujuan untuk merusak reputasi putranya. Administrator kota sedang bekerja sama dengan Departemen Kehakiman untuk membentuk badan pengawas independen yang akan menangani keluhan warga tentang kinerja Kepolisian Sanford. Zimmerman dilaporkan menderita gangguan stres pasca-trauma, depresi, dan insomnia sejak peristiwa penembakan tersebut. article_content: According to Matthew Barzun, the US ambassador to the United Kingdom, Google, Facebook, and Amazon are operating within the established tax regulations and should not be unfairly criticized in Britain. Barzun strongly defended these major American corporations, which have faced considerable scrutiny regarding their tax strategies. He asserted that these companies are simply adhering to the global tax framework established by various governments. In October, David Cameron cautioned that multinational corporations exploiting legal loopholes to evade UK taxes would be compelled to fulfill their tax obligations. The Treasury is set to release information about a new 'Google tax' aimed at ensuring that multinational corporations operating in the UK contribute a minimum level of taxation. However, Barzun conveyed to journalists in Westminster that labeling these firms as 'international tax dodgers' is inaccurate, despite their minimal or nonexistent corporation tax payments in the UK. Barzun clarified, 'I do not represent any of these prominent American companies. These entities, along with others, are adept at utilizing the existing international rules, which, incidentally, were formulated collectively by governmental bodies, including both the US and British governments. They are functioning within these established guidelines. I anticipate that they will continue to comply with any future regulatory changes.' Margaret Hodge, who chairs the Commons public accounts committee and has investigated the tax avoidance tactics employed by some corporations, denounced Barzun's statement as 'a joke'. She argued, 'They are not adhering to the rules as any reasonable person would interpret them. They are manipulating the rules in a manner that is fundamentally unethical. Compliance with the rules entails paying a fair share of taxes in the jurisdictions where revenues are generated. These companies are not doing so, and to suggest that they are complying with the rules is absurd.' The Treasury's impending publication will detail the 'Google tax', intended to guarantee that multinationals operating in the UK pay at least some tax. For instance, Google, which generated over £3.5 billion from the UK in the past year, remitted just over £20 million in corporation tax. Reports indicate that Facebook has paid no corporation tax in the UK for the past two years. Amazon, which recorded £4.3 billion in sales in the UK the previous year, paid only £4.2 million in tax. All three firms maintain that their practices align with international tax regulations. Nevertheless, their actions have incited increasing public discontent in the UK. Chancellor George Osborne announced the prior week that the UK will implement a new 'diverted profits tax' on corporations that attempt to artificially shift their earnings to lower-tax jurisdictions abroad. He estimated that this measure would generate £1 billion over five years. However, experts caution that the 'Google tax', the specifics of which are to be revealed shortly, may prove exceedingly challenging to enforce.
translated_content: Menurut Matthew Barzun, Duta Besar AS untuk Inggris, Google, Facebook, dan Amazon beroperasi sesuai dengan peraturan pajak yang berlaku dan seharusnya tidak dikritik secara tidak adil di Inggris. Barzun dengan tegas membela perusahaan-perusahaan besar Amerika ini, yang telah menghadapi pengawasan ketat terkait strategi pajak mereka. Dia menyatakan bahwa perusahaan-perusahaan ini hanya mematuhi kerangka kerja pajak global yang ditetapkan oleh berbagai pemerintah. Pada bulan Oktober, David Cameron memperingatkan bahwa perusahaan-perusahaan multinasional yang memanfaatkan celah hukum untuk menghindari pajak Inggris akan dipaksa untuk memenuhi kewajiban pajak mereka. Departemen Keuangan akan merilis informasi tentang 'pajak Google' baru yang bertujuan untuk memastikan bahwa perusahaan-perusahaan multinasional yang beroperasi di Inggris memberikan kontribusi pajak minimum. Namun, Barzun menyampaikan kepada wartawan di Westminster bahwa melabeli perusahaan-perusahaan ini sebagai 'penghindar pajak internasional' adalah tidak akurat, meskipun pembayaran pajak korporasi mereka minimal atau bahkan tidak ada di Inggris. Barzun mengklarifikasi, 'Saya tidak mewakili perusahaan-perusahaan Amerika terkemuka ini. Entitas-entitas ini, bersama dengan yang lain, mahir dalam memanfaatkan aturan internasional yang ada, yang kebetulan dirumuskan secara kolektif oleh badan-badan pemerintah, termasuk pemerintah AS dan Inggris. Mereka beroperasi sesuai pedoman yang ditetapkan ini. Saya mengantisipasi bahwa mereka akan terus mematuhi setiap perubahan peraturan di masa depan.' Margaret Hodge, yang memimpin komite rekening publik Commons dan telah menyelidiki taktik penghindaran pajak yang digunakan oleh beberapa perusahaan, mengecam pernyataan Barzun sebagai 'lelucon'. Dia berpendapat, 'Mereka tidak mematuhi aturan seperti yang dipahami oleh orang yang wajar. Mereka memanipulasi aturan dengan cara yang pada dasarnya tidak etis. Kepatuhan terhadap aturan mengharuskan pembayaran pajak yang adil di yurisdiksi tempat pendapatan dihasilkan. Perusahaan-perusahaan ini tidak melakukan itu, dan menyebut mereka mematuhi aturan adalah tidak masuk akal.' Penerbitan yang akan datang dari Departemen Keuangan akan merinci 'pajak Google', yang bertujuan untuk menjamin bahwa perusahaan multinasional yang beroperasi di Inggris membayar setidaknya sejumlah pajak. Contohnya, Google, yang menghasilkan lebih dari £3,5 miliar dari Inggris pada tahun lalu, membayar lebih dari £20 juta dalam pajak korporasi. Laporan menunjukkan bahwa Facebook belum membayar pajak korporasi di Inggris selama dua tahun terakhir. Amazon, yang mencatat penjualan senilai £4,3 miliar di Inggris pada tahun sebelumnya, hanya membayar £4,2 juta dalam pajak. Ketiga perusahaan tersebut menyatakan bahwa praktik mereka selaras dengan peraturan pajak internasional. Meskipun demikian, tindakan mereka telah memicu meningkatnya ketidakpuasan publik di Inggris. Kanselir George Osborne mengumumkan pekan sebelumnya bahwa Inggris akan menerapkan 'pajak pengalihan laba' baru pada perusahaan yang mencoba mengalihkan laba mereka secara artifisial ke yurisdiksi dengan pajak yang lebih rendah di luar negeri. Dia memperkirakan bahwa tindakan ini akan menghasilkan £1 miliar selama lima tahun. Namun, para ahli memperingatkan bahwa 'pajak Google', yang rinciannya akan segera diungkapkan, mungkin akan sangat sulit untuk ditegakkan.

article_content: Danielle Downey, a former LPGA player, tragically passed away at the age of 33 in a car accident. The incident occurred in Auburn, Alabama, when her car veered off Lee Road 57 and collided with a tree after a night out. Reports indicate that Downey lost control of her vehicle around 10pm on Thursday. She was speeding past another driver when the accident happened. The car crashed into a tree, and Downey was ejected as it rolled. Despite being rushed to East Alabama Medical Center, she succumbed to severe head injuries. According to an Alabama Department of Public Safety report, Downey had been out drinking with friends prior to the crash. Her friend, Diana Ramage, reportedly tried to prevent her from driving, concerned about her intoxication. News of Downey's death has deeply affected her family and friends, who remember her for her generosity and dedication. At Auburn University, where she served as the director of golf operations, she was highly regarded. Auburn's golf coach, Kim Evans, expressed her devastation, noting that Downey was like a daughter to her and played a vital role during Evans's illness. Downey, nicknamed 'Deuce', was a three-time All-American and a successful golfer. She is remembered not only for her athletic achievements but also for her kindness and willingness to help others. Auburn athletic director Jay Jacobs described her passing as a tragic loss for the university community, highlighting her impact on the lives of many. Downey is survived by her parents, Mike and Phyllis, and her sisters, Erica Setzer, Melissa Sage, and Shawna Tomasso. She will be remembered for the joy she brought to her nieces and nephews.

Seorang teman dekat, Diana Ramage, bahkan mencoba mengambil kunci mobilnya karena khawatir Downey tidak dalam kondisi yang baik untuk mengemudi. article_content: During his fourth day in Japan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi captivated the Japanese populace with a multifaceted charm offensive. He showcased his affable persona by engaging in various activities, including playing the traditional Japanese Taiko drums, humming 'Vande Mataram,' speaking to scholars at Sacred Heart University about the importance of women's empowerment, and taking selfies with students. In a series of four distinct addresses, Modi positioned India as an ideal investment prospect for Japanese businesses and industry leaders. His day commenced with a speech to female scholars at Sacred Heart University in Tokyo, where he also obliged several ecstatic students by posing for selfies. Following this, upon the Prime Minister's arrival to inaugurate the Vivekanand Centre in Tokyo, enthusiastic chants of 'Har Har Modi' resonated outside the Indian Embassy. Students from schools and colleges, having foregone their classes, waited for hours to catch a glimpse of Modi, who later stepped outside his security perimeter to interact with them and sign autographs. The highlight of the day was Modi's successful attempt at playing the traditional Japanese Taiko drums at the launch of Tata Consultancy Services' (TCS) new initiative for Japanese students. In his business-focused discussions, Modi employed impactful slogans. Addressing prominent figures from Japanese business and industry in a packed hall, he proclaimed, 'There is no red tape, only a red carpet.' Modi presented a '3D formula' for investment, emphasizing India's vibrant democracy, its status as the world's youngest workforce, and the significant demand making it Japan's largest market. Modi conveyed to business leaders that investing in India would be mutually beneficial, highlighting India's considerable advantages for Japan. He suggested that relocating manufacturing to India could substantially reduce costs and potentially yield returns within two years, compared to the decade it might take in Japan. At the inauguration of the TCS Japan Technology and Culture Academy in Tokyo, Modi noted that the overwhelming interest in his address, with over 4,000 applicants for a hall capacity of 2,000, demonstrated Japan's eagerness to deepen its engagement with India. He detailed the potential for substantial returns on Japanese investments, given the size of Indian markets. Citing the metro train system as an example, Modi pointed out that fifty Indian cities are awaiting metro systems, presenting significant investment, manufacturing, and return opportunities. Modi also promoted his 'Make in India' initiative, using Maruti Suzuki as a success story. He encouraged Japanese businesses to invest in India, citing the ease of doing business and promising streamlined processes and support. During his visit, PM Modi humorously questioned whether his presentation of the Srimad Bhagwat Gita to Japan's Emperor Akihito and Prime Minister Shinzo Abe might spark controversy among 'seculars' in India. Speaking to the Indian diaspora in Tokyo, he jokingly remarked that he welcomed such debates, acknowledging the need for everyone to earn a living. He affirmed his commitment to sharing the message of the Bhagwat Gita globally. Enthusiastic chants of 'Har Har Modi, Ghar Ghar Modi' erupted outside the Indian Embassy in Tokyo upon PM Modi's arrival. Schoolchildren, who had waited since 2 pm, expressed their affection for Modi as he interacted with them, signing autographs and inquiring about their studies. Earlier in the day, Modi addressed women scholars at Sacred Heart University, emphasizing the revered status of women in India, comparing them to goddesses such as Saraswati (for education), Lakshmi (for wealth), Annapoorna (for food), and Kali (for safety). He elaborated on initiatives for girls' education, mentioning his auctioning of gifts received as Gujarat CM and donating Rs 78 crore to the Gujarat government for this cause. The article also noted Modi's previous interaction with children at Taimei Elementary School, where he played the flute and shared the story of Lord Krishna. Modi's participation in playing the Taiko drums at the TCS event was described as an unexpected highlight. He listened attentively to a drumming couple before expertly playing the drums himself, leading to enthusiastic applause. Lastly, Prime Minister Narendra Modi met 99-year-old Saichiro Misumi, the oldest living associate of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose in Japan, underscoring historical connections between India and Japan. Modi also requested the Indian Ambassador to Japan to document Misumi's recollections of Bose.

article_content: Shopkeeper John Seabright, 62, successfully fought off two armed raiders who entered his shop by spraying them with cleaning fluid. The incident occurred at the Londis shop in Bourton-on-the-Water, Gloucestershire, where Seabright works. Two masked men, wielding hammers, demanded that Seabright open the till and hand over cash. Seabright initially tried to grab a hammer from one of the robbers but was unsuccessful. He then grabbed a bottle of Mr Muscle surface cleaner and sprayed it into the robbers' eyes through the openings in their balaclavas. The robbers subsequently fled the scene empty-handed, their eyes irritated by the cleaning fluid. Seabright recounted that he initially thought the robbery was a prank. He refused their demands to open the till and told them to leave. A customer attempted to intervene, and Seabright tried to disarm one of the robbers. Seeing the cleaning spray, he used it to incapacitate the raider, leading to their retreat. Jim Wilsdon, 21, was working alongside Seabright during the attempted robbery. CCTV footage captured the robbers entering the store and approaching the counter. The footage shows Seabright spraying the cleaning fluid at one of the raiders. Wilsdon ushered customers, including a woman and her baby, into the bakery for safety. Seabright admitted his hands were shaking when he called 999 but said he wasn't scared. He continued serving customers before the police arrived and returned to work the next day. Store general manager Ewen Smith praised Seabright's instinctive reaction. The robber in the lighter-colored top waited at the door while Seabright sprayed the cleaning fluid. Seabright's wife, Sheila, 70, expressed initial anger and worry but acknowledged her pride in his bravery. She noted the community's positive reaction, with many congratulating Seabright. The first raider was described as being between 5ft 6in and 5ft 11in tall, stocky, and wearing a light grey hooded tracksuit. The second raider was taller and thinner, wearing a light-colored jogging top and bottoms. Police are investigating and have not yet made any arrests. Following the incident, police were called to a similar robbery at a Ladbrokes in Bishop's Cleeve. Two masked robbers threatened a staff member with a hammer and stole a few hundred pounds. Detectives suspect a connection between the two robberies. Gloucestershire Constabulary cautioned against tackling robbers, despite praising Seabright's courage, citing potential dangers.

article_content: The Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) has condemned the 'Kony 2012' campaign as a calculated act of deception, aiming to manipulate global public opinion. This statement, spanning 18 pages, is believed to be their initial response to the viral video that brought attention to the group, led by warlord Joseph Kony. According to the statement, signed by LRA spokesman Justine Labeja, the U.S.A. is the hidden force behind 'Kony 2012.' The LRA views the U.S. as a powerful nation operating an extensive network of military, intelligence, security institutions, and various humanitarian organizations. They allege that Invisible Children, the activist group based in San Diego responsible for the 'Kony 2012' campaign, is one such organization. CNN received the LRA's statement, released on Wednesday, through journalist Frank Nyakairu, along with the email it was sent in. Nyakairu stated that representatives of the LRA in Nairobi, Kenya, who have previously been quoted in international media, sent him the statement. Nyakairu is widely respected for his reporting on the LRA. Although 'Kony 2012' has faced criticism from many sources, this marks the first official response from the LRA. The video detailed the LRA's alleged atrocities over two decades, including the murder and mutilation of villagers, the forced recruitment of child soldiers, and the sexual enslavement of girls. Invisible Children released a follow-up video, 'Beyond Famous,' addressing criticisms of the original 'Kony 2012' video, which became a global phenomenon. The sequel explains the actions taken by politicians in Washington and Africa in response to the campaign. Ben Keesey, the executive director of Invisible Children, stated that the initial video was designed to capture the attention of a young Western audience. He believes the new video provides a more in-depth perspective and will resonate with viewers. Joseph Kony is wanted by the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity. The African Union has announced plans to deploy 5,000 troops to capture him, with assistance from 100 U.S. combat troops dispatched to the region by the Pentagon in October. Kony founded the LRA with the goal of overthrowing the Ugandan government. Since 2006, the LRA has operated in remote areas along the borders of the Central African Republic, South Sudan, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The group has been in retreat since a failed U.S.-backed attack on Kony's position in 2008, known as Operation Lightning Thunder. Since then, LRA attacks have resulted in 2,400 deaths and the displacement of 465,000 people, according to Resolve Uganda. Additionally, 3,400 people have been abducted. The LRA statement also asserts that Invisible Children has been used to conceal the actions of the U.S.-backed Ugandan military. They also accuse Invisible Children co-founder Jason Russell of downplaying the Ugandan military's actions. The LRA statement concludes by calling 'Kony 2012' a deceptive act designed to trick and manipulate the public.

Menurut pernyataan tersebut, yang ditandatangani oleh juru bicara LRA, Justine Labeja, AS adalah kekuatan tersembunyi di balik 'Kony 2012.' LRA memandang AS sebagai negara adikuasa yang mengoperasikan jaringan luas lembaga militer, intelijen, keamanan, dan berbagai organisasi kemanusiaan. Mereka menuduh bahwa Invisible Children, kelompok aktivis yang berbasis di San Diego yang bertanggung jawab atas kampanye 'Kony 2012', adalah salah satu organisasi tersebut. CNN menerima pernyataan LRA, yang dirilis pada hari Rabu, melalui jurnalis Frank Nyakairu, bersama dengan email yang dikirimkan kepadanya. Nyakairu menyatakan bahwa perwakilan LRA di Nairobi, Kenya, yang sebelumnya telah dikutip di media internasional, mengiriminya pernyataan tersebut. Nyakairu sangat dihormati karena liputannya tentang LRA. Meskipun 'Kony 2012' telah menghadapi kritik dari berbagai sumber, ini menandai respons resmi pertama dari LRA. Video tersebut merinci dugaan kekejaman LRA selama lebih dari dua dekade, termasuk pembunuhan dan mutilasi penduduk desa, perekrutan paksa tentara anak-anak, dan perbudakan seksual terhadap anak perempuan. Invisible Children merilis video lanjutan, 'Beyond Famous,' yang menanggapi kritik terhadap video asli 'Kony 2012,' yang menjadi fenomena global. Sekuel ini menjelaskan tindakan yang diambil oleh para politisi di Washington dan Afrika sebagai tanggapan terhadap kampanye tersebut. Ben Keesey, direktur eksekutif Invisible Children, menyatakan bahwa video awal dirancang untuk menarik perhatian audiens muda di Barat. Dia percaya bahwa video baru ini memberikan perspektif yang lebih mendalam dan akan beresonansi dengan pemirsa. Joseph Kony dicari oleh Mahkamah Pidana Internasional atas kejahatan terhadap kemanusiaan. Uni Afrika telah mengumumkan rencana untuk mengerahkan 5.000 tentara untuk menangkapnya, dengan bantuan dari 100 tentara tempur AS yang dikirim ke wilayah tersebut oleh Pentagon pada bulan Oktober. Kony mendirikan LRA dengan tujuan menggulingkan pemerintah Uganda. Sejak 2006, LRA telah beroperasi di daerah-daerah terpencil di sepanjang perbatasan Republik Afrika Tengah, Sudan Selatan, dan Republik Demokratik Kongo. Kelompok ini telah mundur sejak serangan yang gagal yang didukung AS terhadap posisi Kony pada tahun 2008, yang dikenal sebagai Operasi Lightning Thunder. Sejak itu, serangan LRA telah mengakibatkan 2.400 kematian dan pengungsian 465.000 orang, menurut Resolve Uganda. Selain itu, 3.400 orang telah diculik. Pernyataan LRA juga menegaskan bahwa Invisible Children telah digunakan untuk menyembunyikan tindakan militer Uganda yang didukung AS. Mereka juga menuduh salah satu pendiri Invisible Children, Jason Russell, mengecilkan tindakan militer Uganda. Pernyataan LRA menyimpulkan dengan menyebut 'Kony 2012' sebagai tindakan penipuan yang dirancang untuk menipu dan memanipulasi publik.

article_content: Israeli forces issued warnings to Palestinians, urging them to evacuate areas in southern Gaza, possibly indicating an expanded military operation in regions already sheltering displaced individuals. Soldiers are continuing their search of Shifa Hospital in northern Gaza, where they claim to have uncovered weapons but have yet to present evidence of a Hamas command center beneath the complex. Expanding military activities into southern Gaza may worsen the existing humanitarian emergency within the territory. More than 1.5 million people have been displaced within Gaza, with the majority relocating to the south, where essential resources are increasingly limited. The conflict began with a Hamas attack on October 7, resulting in numerous casualties and the capture of hostages. Israel's response includes ongoing air strikes and a ground invasion. Tragically, over 11,200 Palestinians have died, and many remain missing. Gunmen attacked a checkpoint in the West Bank on Thursday. Israeli troops conducted searches at Shifa Hospital and detained technicians, claiming the discovery of weaponry. Hamas and Gaza health officials deny any militant activity within Shifa Hospital. Leaflets were distributed east of Khan Younis, instructing civilians to evacuate. The military claims to have largely secured control of northern Gaza. Residents in Gaza face severe shortages, and the fuel crisis threatens the provision of humanitarian aid. Israel permitted a limited amount of fuel to enter Gaza.

article_content: By Lydia Warren for MailOnline A father has shot dead his wife and their toddler son before turning the gun on himself, police have reported. Brian Miller, 41, was overheard arguing with his wife of five years, 29-year-old Kara Miller, at their home in Spaulding County, Georgia, on Friday, WSBTV reported. When relatives did not hear from the couple over the weekend, they requested a welfare check from the Sheriff's Office, and the three bodies were discovered inside the house on Sunday. It appears that Miller – who relatives described as a religious man – shot his wife and their 21-month-old son, Paxton, in the head with a handgun before killing himself. Scroll down for video Murdered: Kara Miller, left, and 21-month-old Paxton were fatally shot by Brian Miller, right, before he committed suicide. Their bodies were found in their home on Sunday. Disbelief: Family members and neighbors expressed shock that Miller killed his 'perfect' wife and son. Police could not determine how long the bodies had been inside the home. An autopsy will be conducted on the family at the Georgia Bureau of Investigation Crime Lab on Monday, authorities stated. Brian Miller's daughter from a previous relationship told WSBTV that she did not believe her father was responsible for the killings. Ashley Miller, who is pregnant and plans to name her child after her father if it's a boy, said the couple had just celebrated their fifth wedding anniversary and seemed to have a good marriage. Stunning: Kara Miller, a makeup artist in the Atlanta area, posted this photo (right) with her son last month. Loved: Relatives paid tribute to the 'precious' little boy, who was allegedly murdered by his father this weekend. 'I just want to make sure everybody knows he's not that kind of person,' she said. 'He's very involved in the church. He's very religious. He's a good dad, and he didn't deserve something like this.' Neighbors called Kara Miller a perfect wife. 'It's just hard. She was a perfect wife, and he was a perfect son, and if the dad didn't see that he was missing something,' said neighbor Britteny Buck. According to her social media profiles, Kara Miller worked as a freelance hair and makeup artist in the Atlanta metro area. Images also show her posing in model shots or smiling happily with her young son. On Sunday night, her mother, Nancy Sebben, expressed her grief on her Facebook page. Crime scene: They were found by authorities in their home in Spaulding County, Georgia, on Sunday. Shock: Ashley Miller, Miller's daughter from a previous relationship, said she did not think her father was capable of killing his family and insisted he was a religious man and a good father. 'Today my life has changed forever,' she wrote. 'My sweet beautiful daughter Kara and her precious baby Paxton, whom she loved so dearly, were found murdered by her husband. 'My heart is broken beyond repair; no parent should ever be put through such torment. I will die of a broken heart. I loved my babies more than life itself and am thankful I told them every day.'

article_content: A 23-year-old Louisiana woman with a prior DWI charge was arrested on Thursday for claiming to be an employee of the 18th Judicial District Court and attempting to destroy her toxicology report. She called the crime lab from her cell phone and emailed them from her personal account, falsely claiming to be a court employee and requesting the toxicology sample be destroyed because the case had supposedly been dismissed. On April 12, Jana L. Pourciau, 23, of Maringouin, lost control of her Lexus RX350 while driving northbound on LA Hwy 977, south of LA Hwy in Pointe Coupe Parish. Pourciau, who was charged with DWI after the accident, created a fake identity and contacted the crime lab via phone and email to request the destruction of her toxicology report. Pourciau told the crime lab to destroy the toxicology report from her April 12 crash, falsely stating that the case had been dismissed. According to Louisiana State Police officer Jared Sandifer, 'The Lexus ran off the roadway, struck an elementary school fence, and overturned.' Pourciau was initially arrested for DWI, not wearing a seat belt, and careless operation after police suspected she was driving under the influence. She was later arrested for false impersonation and forgery. Nola.com reported that when Pourciau was taken to Baton Rouge Medical Center for her injuries, a toxicology sample was taken. Ten days later, on April 22, Pourciau contacted the Louisiana State Crime Lab from her cell phone using a pseudonym and via email using a fake name. Detectives discovered Pourciau's false phone call and email and brought her in for questioning. Pourciau confessed to calling and emailing the crime lab to destroy the toxicology report related to her crash. She was arrested for false impersonation and forgery and booked into the East Baton Rouge Parish Prison. Police initiated an investigation when they learned Jana Pourciau was trying to destroy toxicology evidence related to her DWI charge. Pourciau confessed to impersonating a court employee to destroy her toxicology report and was arrested for false impersonation and forgery. Pourciau was booked into the East Baton Rouge Parish Prison after impersonating a court employee and attempting to destroy a toxicology report related to her April 12 DWI charge.
